The 1986 Georgia Conflict of Interest Act (O.C.G.A. § 36-67A-1, et seq.) requires disclosure of financial interests by all government officials, including the Mayor and City Council members and Planning and Zoning Commission members, who will consider a rezoning action. It also requires disclosure of campaign contributions or gifts by the rezoning applicant or his/her attorney.
(a) All government officials, including City Council members and Planning and Zoning Commission members, are required to disclose in writing any ownership interest they have or any family members have, in real property made the subject of a rezoning request. Additionally, these officials are required to disclose in writing any financial interest of ten percent or more in any business entity which has an ownership interest in the property to be considered.
(b) An applicant for a rezoning and his/her attorney must disclose all campaign contributions or gifts aggregating $250.00 or more which were made within two years of the filing of the application for rezoning.

The following words shall have the following meaning for the purpose of this Ordinance:
2.1.1 Acceleration lane: An added roadway lane, of a specified distance and which may include a taper, as approved by the City's Engineer, that permits vehicles to speed up and enter the main vehicle stream.
2.1.2 Accessory building: A subordinate building or structure on the same lot as the main building and devoted exclusively to an accessory use. (See also: Building, Accessory Residential and Building, Accessory Commercial).
2.1.3 Accessory building, portable: An accessory building temporarily located on a site of construction or located on a residential lot.
2.1.4 Accessory building, stationary: A fixed accessory building placed on the side or rear yard after completion of the principle building on the lot.
2.1.5 Accessory use: A use that is customarily incidental, appropriate and subordinate to the principal use of land or building(s) and that is located upon the same lot therewith. Residential accessory use shall not involve the conduct of business.
2.1.6 Adult entertainment: Performances by topless and/or bottomless dancers, strippers or similar entertainers, where such performances are characterized by the display or exposure of specified anatomical areas.
2.1.7 Adult entertainment establishment: Adult entertainment establishments include, but are not limited to:
(a) Adult bookstore: A business or establishment having a substantial or significant portion of its stock in trade in books, magazines, periodicals, novelty items, sex toys, or accessories which are distinguished or characterized by their emphasis on matter depicting, describing or relating to specified sexual activities or specified anatomical areas or an establishment with a segment or section, comprising five percent or more of its total floor space, devoted to the sale or display of such material, or having five percent or more of its net sales consisting of material or items which are distinguished or characterized by their emphasis on matter depicting, describing or relating to specified sexual activities or specified anatomical areas.
(b) Adult business: Either (1) any business or establishment which is conducted exclusively for the patronage of adults and as to which minors are specifically excluded from patronage either by law or by the operators of such business or establishment; or (2) any business or establishment to which the public or any portion thereof is permitted where employees or patrons expose specified anatomical areas or engage in specified sexual activities; or (3) any other business or establishment to which the public or any portion thereof is permitted which offers its patrons services or entertainment characterized by an emphasis on matter depicting, describing, discussing or relating to specified sexual activities or specified anatomical areas.
(c) Adult dancing establishment: A business or establishment that features live performances by topless and/or bottomless dancers, go-go dancers, strippers or similar entertainers, where such performances are distinguished or characterized by an emphasis on specified sexual activities or specified anatomical areas.
(d) Adult motion picture theater: A business or establishment that is used for presenting material distinguished or characterized by an emphasis on matter depicting, describing, or relating to specified sexual activities or specified anatomical areas for observation by patrons therein, including a business or establishment wherein coin or slug operated or electronically, electrically or mechanically controlled still or motion picture machines, projectors or other image producing devices are maintained to show images and where the images so displayed are distinguished or characterized by an emphasis on, depicting or describing specified sexual activities or specified anatomical areas.
(e) Adult video store: A business or establishment having a substantial or significant portion of its stock in trade in DVDs, video tapes, movies or other reproductions, for sale or rent, which are distinguished or characterized by their emphasis on matter depicting, describing or relating to specified sexual activities or specified anatomical areas or an establishment with a segment or section, comprising five percent or more of its total floor space, devoted to the sale or rental of such material, or having five percent or more of its net sales consisting of reproduced materials which are distinguished or characterized by their emphasis on matter depicting, describing or relating to specified sexual activities or specified anatomical areas.
(f) Bath house or massage parlor: A business or establishment in which services offered include some form of physical contact between employee and patron and in which services offered are characterized or distinguished by an emphasis on specified sexual activities or specified anatomical areas.
(g) Erotic entertainment/dance establishment: A business or establishment including, but not limited to, a nightclub, bar, restaurant, theater, or other establishment which features live performances by topless and/or bottomless dancers or entertainers, go-go dancers, strippers or similar entertainers, where such performances are distinguished or characterized by an emphasis on specified sexual activities or specified anatomical areas.
(h) Lingerie modeling studio: A business or establishment whose primary business activity consists of live performers exhibiting or modeling lingerie or similar undergarments and are characterized or distinguished by an emphasis on specified sexual activities or specified anatomical areas.
(i) Encounter center or rap establishment: A business, agency or person who, for any form of consideration or gratuity, provides a place where two or more persons may congregate, assemble or associate for the primary purpose of engaging in, describing or discussing specified sexual activities, or exposing specified anatomical areas.
2.1.8 Agriculture: Improvements and activities associated with the raising and harvesting of crops and/or livestock. "Agriculture" includes ancillary activities, including equipment storage and repair, packing, treating or storing produce; provided, however, that the operation of any such accessory uses shall be secondary to that of normal agricultural activities. Exception: the raising of hogs, pigs or other livestock fed from garbage or nonmuscular animal parts, or other agricultural uses that produce noxious odors are excluded from this definition.
2.1.9 Alley: A strip of land dedicated to public use providing vehicular and pedestrian access to the rear of properties which abut and are served by a public road or street.
2.1.10 Amendment: Any repeal, modification or addition to a regulation; a new regulation; any change in the numbers, shape, boundary or area of a district or any repeal or abolition of any map, part thereof, or addition thereto.
2.1.11 Antenna: Any system of wires, poles, towers, rods, discs, dishes, or similar devices used for the transmission or reception of electromagnetic waves attached to the exterior of a building or mounted in the ground independent (freestanding) of a building on a tower or pole.
2.1.12 Apartment: A room or suite of one or more rooms with a private bathroom which is designed or intended for occupancy by, or which is occupied by, one family doing its own cooking therein, or by one person doing his/her own cooking therein.
2.1.13 Apartment house: Any building or portion thereof which contains three or more apartments, the occupants of any two or more of which use any entrance or hall in common and all living units of which are intended to be maintained under single ownership.
2.1.14 Applicant, development: The owner of land proposed to be subdivided or his/her representative who shall have express written authority to act on behalf of the owner.
2.1.15 Appurtenance: In general, appurtenances include without limitation appendages to the original structure such as: additions, mechanical systems, covered walkways, satellite dishes and antennae, attached storage buildings, attached parking decks, etc. In site planning, the term appurtenance may be applied to access roads and parking areas as well.
2.1.16 Arterial: A class of roads serving major traffic movements (high-speed, high volume) for travel between major points.
2.1.17 Automobile sales or storage yard: An open premises used for the storage of or sale of complete and operable automobiles.
2.1.18 Automobile service station: A building, lot or both in or upon which minor and emergency repair services may be rendered along with gasoline sales. Services are not to include major mechanical and/or body work.
2.1.19 Base flood: The flood having a one percent chance of being equaled or exceeded in any given year. Also known as the 100-year flood.
2.1.20 Basement: A room or story partly underground, and having at least one-half of its height above the average level of the adjoining ground. A basement shall be counted as a story if used for dwelling or business purposes.
2.1.21 Billboard: Any display indicating the business transacted, services rendered, goods sold or produced, name of business, person, firm or corporation which is not available or located on the same premises as the display.
2.1.22 Block: An area of land that is entirely surrounded by public streets, public lands, railroad rights-of-way, watercourses, or other well defined and fixed boundaries. (See Figure 2.1.A.)
Figure 2.1.A Block
2.1.23 Boarding house: A residential use consisting of at least one dwelling unit together with more than two rooms that are rented or are designed or intended to be rented but which rooms, individually or collectively, do not constitute separate dwelling units. A rooming house or boarding house is distinguished from a Bed and Breakfast in that the former is designed to be occupied by longer term residents (at least month-to-month tenants) as opposed to overnight or weekly guests.
2.1.24 Bond: Any form of security including a cash deposit, surety bond, collateral, property or instrument of credit in an amount and form satisfactory to the Governing Body. All bonds shall be approved by the City of Wrens wherever a bond is required by these regulations.
2.1.25 Buffer: Landscaped, fenced or walled area which forms a linear stretch abutting a property line, pavement or structure.
2.1.26 Buildable area: That portion of any lot which may be used or built upon in accordance with the regulations governing the given zoning district within which the particular lot is located, once the various front, side and rear building line setbacks required for the land use have been subtracted from the total area.
2.1.27 Building: A structure having a roof supported by columns or walls for the shelter, support or enclosure of persons, animals or personal property. When separated without connections, each portion of such building shall be deemed a separate building.
2.1.28 Building, accessory commercial: In the nonresidential districts, a subordinate building to the main building that does not exceed the height of the main building and does not exceed 50 percent of the heated ground floor area of the main building, and that is used for purposes accessory and incidental to the main use. (See: Accessory Use).
2.1.29 Building, accessory residential: In a residential district, a subordinate building that is attached or detached to the main structure or building and is used for a purpose that is customarily incidental to the main structure but not involving the conduct of a business. The total square footage of all accessory buildings must be less than 50 percent of the heated ground floor area of the main structure. Examples include, but are not limited to, the following: a private garage for automobile storage, tool shed, greenhouse as a hobby (no business), home workshop, children's playhouse, guesthouse, storage building, garden shelter, etc. (See: Accessory Use; Guesthouse).
Figure 2.1.B Building Height
2.1.30 Building Department: The Building Department of Jefferson County, Georgia. A sub-department of the Tax Assessors Office of Jefferson County, Georgia.
2.1.31 Building height: The vertical distance measured from the level of the established grade opposite the middle of the front of the building, to the highest point of the roof surface if a flat roof; to the deck line of a mansard roof; and to the mean height level between eaves and ridge for a gable, hip or gambrel roof. In case of a through lot or double frontage lot as defined in section 2.1.123, the established grade of such abutting street shall govern to one half the depth of the lot. (See Figures 2.1.B and 2.1.C.)
Figure 2.1.C Roof Types
2.1.32 Building Inspector: The office or person duly appointed or authorized by City Council to inspect buildings and structures in accordance with the provisions of this Ordinance or any other City ordinance or regulation.
2.1.33 Building line: A line, other than a lot line, used to regulate the location of a building or structure in relation to the abutting street or streets. (See Figure 2.1.G.)
2.1.34 Building line, front: A line, other than a lot line, used to regulate the location of a building or structure in relation to the abutting street or streets on the front of a lot. (See Figure 2.1.G.)
2.1.35 Building line, side: A line, other than a lot line, used to regulate the location of a building or structure in relation to the abutting street or streets on the side of a lot. (See Figure 2.1.G.)
2.1.36 Building line, rear: A line, other than a lot line, used to regulate the location of a building or structure in relation to the abutting street or streets on the rear of a lot. (See Figure 2.1.G.)
2.1.37 Building line setback: The distance between the building line and the right-of-way in a district, lot, tract or parcel of land. (See Figure 2.1.G.)
2.1.38 Building site: The ground area of a building or buildings together with all open spaces surrounded by said building or buildings.
2.1.39 Cellar: A portion of a building having one-half or more of its height below the average grade of the adjoining ground.
2.1.40 Certificate of occupancy (C.O.): Official certification of a building's compliance with building regulations. When the occupancy type of a building is changed or when an addition or new building is completed, a Certificate of Occupancy must be obtained before the structure can legally be occupied.
2.1.41 Child care facility, commercial: A building or structure operated by any person or company where care and supervision of children is provided for a fee to more than 12 children, including children of the adult provider.
2.1.42 City: The City of Wrens, Georgia.
2.1.43 City Attorney: The attorney contracted by the City to perform legal duties.
2.1.44 City Clerk: The individual appointed by Mayor and City Council to perform the duties of the City Clerk.
2.1.45 City Council: The Mayor and City Council of the City of Wrens, Georgia.
2.1.46 City's Engineer: The licensed engineer or engineering firm contracted by the City to perform engineering duties.
2.1.47 Club, church or fraternal organization: Buildings and facilities owned or operated by a corporation, association, person or persons for a social, civic, educational, religious or recreational purpose, but not operated primarily for profit or to render a service which is customarily a business.
2.1.48 Commercial group development: A development consisting of one or more lots developed as a cohesive project and designed with a blend of various compatible commercial uses. The uses may be located in the same building or in separate buildings.
2.1.49 Commercial use: Any use involving in part or in whole, the storage of merchandise, sale of merchandise, materials or services, but not including Home Occupations, as defined in 2.1.98.
2.1.50 Commission: The Planning and Zoning Commission of the City of Wrens, Georgia.
2.1.51 Common line: A property line shared between two parcels or tracts of property.
2.1.52 Comprehensive Plan: Any plan adopted by the City Council of the City of Wrens, or a portion of such plan or plans. This definition shall be construed liberally to include a major thoroughfare plan, master parks and recreation plan, or any other study, document, or written recommendation pertaining to subjects normally within the subject matter of a Comprehensive Plan, if formally adopted by the City.
2.1.53 Conditional use: A use permitted in a particular zoning district only upon showing that such use in a specific location will comply with all of the conditions and standards for the location or operation of such use as specified in this Ordinance and as authorized by the City Council.
2.1.54 Condominium: A common-interest community in which portions of the real estate are designated for separate ownership and the remainder of the real estate is designated for common ownership solely by the owners of those portions. A common-interest community is not a condominium unless the undivided interests in the common elements are vested in the units' owners.
2.1.55 Conservation areas, primary: Any property qualifying as conservation use property under O.C.G.A. § 48-5-7.4; and any steep mountain slopes, floodplains, wetlands, waterbodies, upland buffers around wetlands and waterbodies, critical wildlife habitat, and sites of historic, cultural, or archaeological significance, located outside of building areas and lots established for building purposes.
2.1.56 Conservation areas, secondary: Prime farmland, natural meadows, mature woodlands, farm fields, localized aquifer recharge areas, and lands containing scenic views and sites, located outside of existing buildings and lots established for building purposes.
2.1.57 Conservation easement: A legally enforceable agreement between a property owner and the holder of the easement, in a form acceptable to the City Attorney and recorded in the office of the Clerk of Superior Court of Jefferson County. A conservation easement restricts the existing and future use of the defined tract or lot to conservation use, agriculture, passive recreation, or other use approved by City Council and prohibits further subdivision or development. Such agreement may also provide for the maintenance of open spaces and any improvements on the tract or lot. Such agreement cannot be altered except with the express written permission of the easement holder. A conservation easement may also establish other provisions and contain standards that safeguard the tracts or lots special resources from negative changes.
2.1.58 Construction plan: The maps and/or drawings accompanying a subdivision plat or plan which show the specific location and design of improvements to be installed in the subdivision in accordance with the requirements of the Commission as a condition of the approval of the plat or plan.
2.1.59 Contiguous common parcels: Parcels adjoining or touching other land at a common point and having a common owner, regardless of whether or not portions of the parcels have separate tax identification numbers, or were purchased in different land lots, or were purchased at different times.
2.1.60 Convenience store: Any retail establishment offering for sale prepackaged food products, household items and other goods commonly associated with the same and having a gross floor area of less than 5,000 square feet.
2.1.61 Corridor: The area abutting the right-of-way along streets, roads, highways or interstates with the depth of that area being established by a boundary line on the zoning map. The area generally consists of the viewshed, meaning that area visible from the road.
2.1.62 Corridor Design Overlay District: A gateway or entrance corridor to the City where additional design criteria is required to protect and improve the character of the district while directing future development in harmony with the unique status of the City of Wrens.
2.1.63 Cul-de-sac: A street that terminates in a vehicular turn around at the termination of a street or alley.
2.1.64 Cul-de-sac, temporary: A nonpermanent vehicular turn around located at the termination of a street or alley.
2.1.65 Day care center: A facility in which supervision and/or treatment is regularly provided for compensation to five or more adult persons not related to the proprietor.
2.1.66 Deceleration lane: An added roadway lane, of a specified distance and which may include a taper, as approved by the City's Engineer, which permits vehicles to slow down and leave the main vehicle stream.
2.1.67 Dedication plat: A plat that indicates property to be dedicated for public right-of-way or land for public use.
2.1.68 Dedication: The deliberate appropriation of land by an owner for any general and public use or purpose, reserving to himself no other rights than such as are compatible with the full exercise and enjoyment of the public uses to which the property has been devoted.
2.1.69 Developer: A person or entity responsible for any undertaking that requires a Building Permit, Conditional Use Permit or Sign Permit.
2.1.70 Development: Any manmade change on improved or unimproved real estate, including but not limited to, buildings, structures, mining, dredging, filling, grading, paving, excavation, drilling, or permanent storage of materials or equipment.
2.1.71 Dimensional nonconformity: A nonconforming situation that occurs when the height, size or minimum floor space of a structure or the relationship between an existing building or buildings and other buildings or lot lines does not conform to the regulations applicable to the district in which the property is located.
2.1.72 Display area, sign: The area of the smallest horizontally or vertically oriented rectangle which could enclose all the display area of a sign, together with any backing different in color or material from the finished material of the building face without deduction for open space or other irregularities. Structural members not bearing advertising matter shall not be included unless internally or decoratively lighted. Only one side of flat back-to-back signs need be included in calculating sign display area.

R-1 Single-Family Residential (low density, ½ acre minimum lot area)
R-1A Single-Family Residential (high density, ⅓ acre minimum lot area)

2.1.74 Dripline: The periphery of the area beneath a tree that would be encompassed by perpendicular lines dropped from the furthermost edges of the crown of the tree.
2.1.75 Driveway: A privately-owned vehicular passageway having at least one end thereof connected to a public street, and providing ingress to and/or egress from a lot.
2.1.76 Dwelling: Any building or portion thereof, which is designed or used exclusively for residential purposes.
2.1.77 Dwelling, single-family: A structure containing not more than one dwelling unit designed for residential use, which meets or exceeds the following standards:
(a) Minimum width in excess of 16 feet;
(b) Minimum square footage required by the zoning district in which located;
(c) The roof shall have a minimum 2:12 (two inches of rise for every 12 inches of run) roof pitch and shall have a surface of wood shakes, asphalt composition, wood shingles, concrete, fiberglass or metal tiles, slate, built-up gravel materials, or other materials approved by the Building Inspector;
(d) The exterior siding materials shall consist of wood, masonry, concrete, stucco, masonite, or vinyl or other materials of like appearance;
(e) The dwelling is attached to a permanent foundation.
2.1.78 Dwelling, two-family: A building containing not more than two dwelling units, and designed or used to house not more than two families, living independently of each other, and each having its own kitchen and bath, each of which may include no more than two lodgers or boarders.
2.1.79 Dwelling, multi-family: A building designed for, or portion of a building having accommodations for three or more families living independently of each other, and each having its own kitchen and bath facilities. This term includes dwellings occupied more or less permanently for residential purposes in which the rooms are occupied in apartments, suites or groups such as apartment units, flats, bachelor apartments, studio apartments, kitchenette apartments, townhouses and other buildings similarly occupied.
2.1.80 Dwelling unit: A structure or a portion of any structure designed, arranged and used for living quarters for one or more persons living as a single housekeeping unit with bathroom and cooking facilities, but not including units in hotels, motels, boarding houses or similar uses.
2.1.81 Easement: A grant of one or more property rights by the property owner to and/or for use by the public, a corporation, or another person or entity. (See Figure 2.1.D.)
Figure 2.1.D Easements
2.1.82 Escrow account: A type of subdivision improvement guarantee where the subdivider deposits cash, a note, a bond, or some other instrument readily convertible to cash for specific face value, as specified by the City's Engineer, to cover the costs of required improvements.
2.1.83 Exterior architectural feature: The architectural style, general design, and general arrangement of the exterior of a structure, including, but not limited to, the texture of the building material, the type and style of all windows, doors, and signs, and other related architectural fixtures, features, details, or elements.
2.1.84 Family: One or more persons having a common domestic bond who live together in one dwelling unit as a traditional family or its functional equivalent, headed by one or more resident persons who have authority over the care, functioning or management of their common household. The definition of a "Family" does not include:
(a) Any society, club, fraternity, sorority, association, lodge, combine, federation, coterie, or like organization;
(b) Any group of individuals whose association is temporary or seasonal in nature; or
(c) Any group of individuals who are in a group living arrangement as a result of criminal offenses.
2.1.85 Fenestration: The spatial definition of the walls of a building. The facade of a building establishes a wall surface or plane. The degree to which that plane is visually segmented by bays and punctured by entrances and windows is fenestration. For example, historic buildings have a high degree of fenestration and large, modern "big-box" stores have an extremely low degree of fenestration. The City's architectural history is one of moderate to high fenestration.
2.1.86 Final plat: The final drawing of a subdivision and, as applicable, dedication, prepared for filing for record with the Clerk of the Jefferson County Superior Court, and containing all elements and requirements set forth in this Ordinance.
2.1.87 Floodplain: Any land area susceptible to be inundated by water from the Base Flood. As used in this Ordinance, the term refers to that area designated as subject to flooding from the Base Flood (100-year flood) on the "Flood Boundary and Floodway Map" prepared by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. (See: Base Flood).
2.1.88 Floodway: The channel of a river or other watercourse and the adjacent land areas that must be reserved in order to discharge the base flood without cumulatively increasing the water surface elevation more than one foot. As used in this Ordinance, the term refers to that area designated as a floodway on the "Flood Boundary and Floodway Map" prepared by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. (See: Base Flood).
2.1.89 Gateway: Distinct corners, formed by the intersections of major streets, arteries, and highways, which mark the established edge of the community and distinguish the route entering the heart of the community.
2.1.90 Garage: A building used for the storage or housing of motor vehicles.
2.1.91 Garage, private: A garage intended for an owner or used by the members of families resident upon the premises. No rental of private garage space is permitted.
2.1.92 Grade: The slope of a road, street, or other public way, specific in percentage terms from the horizontal.
2.1.93 Gross floor area: The total area of a building measured by taking the outside dimensions of the building at each floor level intended for occupancy or storage.
2.1.94 Guest house: An accessory building to be used solely by the occupant of the main building for his/her pleasure or recreation or to house non-paying guests or tenants as a temporary residence. Guest Houses shall meet the same square footage requirement as Accessory Buildings: the total square footage of the guesthouse and all accessory buildings must be less than 50 percent of the heated ground floor area of the main structure. (See also: Building, Accessory Residential, Section 2.1.29).
2.1.95 Habitat for endangered or threatened species: An area verified by the Georgia Department of Natural Resources as: (a) actually containing naturally-occurring individuals of a species that has been listed as endangered or threatened under the Federal Endangered Species Act, as amended; and (b) being likely to support the continued existence of that species by providing for a significant portion of that species' biological requirements, and that meets the definition of "Natural Conditions" as defined by this Ordinance.
2.1.96 Habitable floor: Any floor usable for living purposes, which includes working, sleeping, eating, cooking, or recreation, or any combination thereof. A floor having the limited purpose of storage is not a habitable floor.
2.1.97 Health Department: The Health Department of Jefferson County, Georgia.
2.1.98 Home occupation: Any occupation or profession engaged in by any occupant of a dwelling not to include the operation of a retail business, a manufacturing business or a repair business of any kind on the premises. Home Occupation shall not include any occupation conducted in any building on the premises other than the building which is used by the occupant as his/her private dwelling. Home occupation shall include, in general, personal services such as those furnished by a musician, internet business, artist, barber, hairstylist, beautician or seamstress when performed by the person occupying the building as his/her private dwelling. Home occupation shall not include occupations that involve the use of chemicals, matter or energy that may create or cause to be created noises, noxious odors or hazards that will endanger the health, safety and welfare of the community. (See also: Section 22.1).
2.1.99 Homeowners association: An organization formed for the maintenance and operation of the common areas of a development, where membership in the association is automatic with the purchase of a dwelling unit or lot within the development, with the ability to legally assess fees to each owner of a dwelling unit or lot and which has authority to place a lien against all dwelling units and lots within the development.
2.1.100 Hospital: An institution providing primary health services and medical or surgical care to persons, primarily inpatients suffering from illness, disease, injury, deformity and other abnormal physical or mental conditions, and including, as an integral part of the institution, related facilities such as laboratories, outpatient facilities or training facilities.
2.1.101 Hospital, animal: A place where animals are given medical or surgical treatment and the boarding of animals is incidental to the hospital use. All facilities associated with an Animal Hospital shall be located indoors.
2.1.102 Hotel: Any building which contains multiple sleeping rooms for the more or less temporary occupancy of individuals who are lodged with or without meals.
2.1.103 HUD: The U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.
2.1.104 Individual sewage disposal system: A septic tank, seepage tile sewage disposal system, or any other sewage treatment device.
2.1.105 Industrialized building: Any structure or component thereof which is wholly or in substantial part made, fabricated, formed or assembled in manufacturing facilities for installation on a building site and has been manufactured in such a manner that all parts or processes cannot be inspected at the installation site without disassembly, damage to or destruction thereof. Industrialized buildings are constructed and regulated in accordance with the Industrialized Buildings Act, O.C.G.A. § 8-2-110, et seq. (See also: Modular Building).
2.1.106 Interior landscaping: Landscaping areas within or partially within pavement areas for breaking up large expanses of pavement. Interior landscape areas include islands, peninsulas, or combinations thereof.
2.1.107 Island: An interior landscaping area surrounded by pavement or structures.
2.1.108 Junk yard: The use of more than 200 square feet of the area of any lot for outdoor storage, keeping or abandonment of junk, including scrap metals or other scrap materials, or for the dismantling, demolition or abandonment of automobiles, vehicles, or machinery or parts thereof. (See also: Section 7.3.5).
2.1.109 Kennel: An establishment licensed to operate a facility housing dogs, cats, or other household pets and where grooming, breeding, boarding, training, or selling of animals is conducted as a business.
2.1.110 Land suitability analysis: A method used by land planners, in preparing land use plans at a community-wide scale or land plans at a site development scale, to evaluate the fitness of land for various uses based at least partially on environmental criteria. The end product of land suitability analysis is typically a map or set of maps depicting the appropriateness of land areas for various land uses.
2.1.111 Land use permit: A permit issued to authorize the use of land or development of land for a specific purpose.
2.1.112 Landscape, frontage: Landscape areas between the front of the principal building(s) and adjacent street(s).
2.1.113 Landscape, perimeter: Landscape areas located between the side(s) and rear of the primary building(s) and adjacent property line(s).
2.1.114 Landscaping: Landscaping shall consist of any of the following or combination thereof: material such as, but not limited to, grass, ground covers, shrubs, flowers, vines, hedges, trees, native plant materials, planters, brick, stone or natural forms, water forms, aggregate or other landscape features, but not including the use of smooth concrete or asphalt. The use of brick, stone, aggregate or other inorganic materials should not predominate over the use of organic plant material.
2.1.115 Lane: A public thoroughfare which ordinarily affords only a secondary means of access to abutting property and which is not more than 25 feet wide.
2.1.116 Letter of credit: A type of subdivision improvement guarantee whereby a subdivider secures an instrument from a bank or other institution or from a person with resources sufficient to cover the cost of improvements required by the City. The instrument pledges the creditor to pay the cost of improvements in case of default by the subdivider.
2.1.117 Living quarters: Any habitable area used for lodging.
2.1.118 Loading area: A parking area other than a public street used for the purpose of loading or unloading material, merchandise, or persons.
2.1.119 Lot: A portion or parcel of land separated from other portions or parcels by description (such as on a subdivision plat or a survey map or plat) or described by metes and bounds, and intended for use, transfer of ownership, or for building development. The word "lot" shall not include any portion of a right-of-way. (See Figure 2.1.E.)

2.1.120 Lot area: The total area included within the front, side and rear lot lines. (See Figure 2.1.F.)
Figure 2.1.F Lot Definitions.
2.1.121 Lot, corner: A lot abutting upon two or more streets at their intersection. (See Figure 2.1.E.)
2.1.122 Lot, depth: The average horizontal distance between the front and rear lot lines. (See Figure 2.1.F and 2.1.H)
2.1.123 Lot, double frontage: A lot other than a corner lot that has frontage upon two or more streets that do not intersect at a point abutting the property. (See Figure 2.1.E.)
2.1.124 Lot, flag: Flag Lots are prohibited by this Ordinance. A flag lot is a tract or lot of land of uneven dimensions in which the portion fronting on a street is less than the required minimum width required for construction of a building or structure on that lot. (See Figure 2.1.E.)
2.1.125 Lot frontage: The width in linear feet of a lot where it abuts the right-of-way of any street. (See Figure 2.1.F.)
2.1.126 Lot improvement: Any building, structure, place, work of art, sign, or other object, or improvement of the land on which they are situated constituting a physical betterment of real property, or any part of such betterment.
2.1.127 Lot, interior: A lot which is not a corner lot. (See Figure 2.1 .E.)
2.1.128 Lot line, front: The front lot line of an interior lot separating the lot from the fronting street right-of-way. The front lot line of a corner lot shall be the lot line upon which the principal building entrance will front. (See Figure 2.1 .G.)
2.1.129 Lot line, rear: The rear lot line boundary opposite and more or less parallel to the front lot line. The rear lot line of an irregular or triangular lot shall be for the purpose of this Ordinance a line not less than ten feet long, lying wholly within the lot, and parallel to the farthest distance from the front lot line. (See Figure 2.1.G.)
2.1.130 Lot line, side: A side lot boundary line that is not a front lot line or a rear lot line. A side lot line separating a lot from a street line is an exterior side lot line. Any other side lot line is an interior side lot line. (See Figure 2.1.G.)
Figure 2.1.G Lot Lines
2.1.131 Lot of record: A lot which is part of a subdivision approved in accordance with the land subdivision requirements of this Ordinance or a lot described on a plat, deed or survey which has been lawfully recorded in the property records of the Clerk of the Jefferson County Superior Court.
2.1.132 Lot, through: (See: Lot Double Frontage).
2.1.133 Lot width: The shortest distance between side lot lines measured at the regulatory/required front building line, or in the absence of a front building line, the distance between side lot lines measured at the front line of the building located or intended to be located on the lot. (See Figures 2.1.F and 2.1.H.)

2.1.134 Manufactured home: A structure, transportable in one or more sections, which, in traveling mode, is eight body feet or more in width or 40 body feet or more in length, when erected on site, is 320 or more square feet in floor area, and which is built on a permanent chassis and designed to be used as a dwelling with or without a permanent foundation when connected to the required utilities, and includes the plumbing, heating, air-conditioning, and electrical systems contained therein; or a structure that otherwise comes within the definition of a "manufactured home" under the National Manufactured Housing Construction and Safety Standards Act of 1974, as amended (42 U.S.C. §5401-5426).
2.1.135 Manufactured home community: A contiguous parcel of land under single ownership which has been planned and improved for the placement of three or more Manufactured Homes for residential occupancy in accordance with Article 16 of this Ordinance. The owner must obtain an Occupation Tax Certificate from the City of Wrens prior to operating a Manufactured Home Community.
2.1.136 Manufactured home site: A lot, as prescribed by Article 15, Section 15.5(b) of this Ordinance which shall be clearly indicated by corner markers on which may be placed a Manufactured Home.
2.1.137 Marquee: A permanent structure attached to and supported by a building which projects over public or private property.
2.1.138 Material change in appearance: The construction of a new structure, or a change that will affect the exterior architectural features of any structure, site, or work of art. Ordinary maintenance or repair of any exterior architectural feature in or on a structure that does not involve a change in design is not a "material change in appearance." Material change in appearance includes without limitation any one or more of the following:
(a) A reconstruction or alteration of the size, shape, or facade of a structure, including without limitation relocation of any doors or windows, or removal or alteration of any architectural features, details, or elements;
(b) Demolition of a structure;
(c) Commencement of excavation;
(d) A change in the location of advertising visible from the public way on the property; or
(e) The erection, alteration, restoration, or removal of any structure, including walls, fences, steps, and pavements, or other related features.
2.1.139 Mayor: The Mayor of the City of Wrens, Georgia.
2.1.140 Mobile office unit: A transportable, factory-assembled unit designed as temporary office facilities for construction projects or temporary offices associated with commercial, industrial, business or institutional activities.
2.1.141 Modular building: A structure constructed in a factory of factory assembled parts, transported to the building site in whole or in units and later attached to a permanent foundation. The completed structure is not a mobile home or a Manufactured Home. (See also: Industrialized Building).
2.1.142 Motel: Any building containing multiple sleeping rooms for more or less temporary occupancy of individuals who are lodged with or without meals and where the design favors a direct vehicular approach to each sleeping or living room. Any building or structure used primarily as temporary lodging and exceeding two stories in height shall be classified as a Hotel rather than a Motel.
2.1.143 Mural: A pictorial representation not specifically identifying goods or services offered by the business on the premises.
2.1.144 Natural conditions: The flora, fauna, soil and water conditions that would develop on a specific tract of land if all human interference were to be removed. The tract of land must have been undisturbed for a sufficient period of time for natural processes to dominate the tract. This period of time will vary among environments.
2.1.145 Natural grade: The elevation of the ground adjoining the building.
2.1.146 Nonconforming lot: A lot existing at the effective date of this Ordinance (and not created for the purposes of evading the restrictions of this Ordinance) that does not meet the minimum area requirements of the zoning district in which the lot is located.
2.1.147 Nonconforming situation: A situation that occurs when, on the effective date of this Ordinance, any existing lot or structure or use of an existing lot or structure does not conform to one or more of the regulations applicable to the zoning district in which the lot or structure is located. Among other possibilities, a non-conforming situation may arise when an existing structure exceeds the maximum height limitation, when the relationship between existing buildings and the land (in such matters as density and setback requirements) is not in conformity with this Ordinance, or when land or buildings are used for purposes made unlawful by this Ordinance. Nonconforming signs shall be governed by the provisions of Section 17.13 of this Ordinance.
2.1.148 Nonconforming use: A use or activity that was lawful prior to the adoption, revision or amendment of this Ordinance but that fails by reason of such adoption, revision or amendment to conform to the present requirements of the zoning district.
2.1.149 Nudity: The displaying of any portion of the female breast below the top of the areola or the displaying of any portion of a person's pubic hair, anus, cleft of the buttocks, vulva, or genitals.
2.1.150 Nursing care home: A facility maintained for the purpose of providing skilled nursing care and medical supervision at a lower level than that available in a hospital.
2.1.151 Obscene: Material is obscene if:
(a) To the average person, applying contemporary community standards, taken as a whole, it predominantly appeals to the prurient interest, that is, a shameful or morbid interest in nudity, sex, or excretion; and
(b) The material taken as a whole lacks serious literary, artistic, political, or scientific value; and
(c) The material depicts or describes, in a patently offensive way, any of the following sexual conduct:
(1) Acts of sexual intercourse, heterosexual or homosexual, normal or perverted, actual or simulated;
(2) Acts of masturbation;
(3) Acts involving excretory functions or lewd exhibition of the genitals;
(4) Acts of bestiality or the fondling of sex organs of animals; or
(5) Sexual acts of flagellation, torture, or other violence indicating a sadomasochistic sexual relationship.
2.1.152 Off-premises sign: Signs directing attention to a business or service not related to the premises on which the sign is located.
2.1.153 On-premises sign: Signs identifying or related to a business or service located on the premises where the sign is located.
2.1.154 Open space: Any combination of Primary Conservation Areas and Secondary Conservation Areas, as defined in this Ordinance, that together form a permanent, undivided or relatively undivided, undeveloped area. As much as 25 percent of the open space may be devoted to Active Recreation facilities, as defined in this Ordinance. Easements for electric transmission lines or any other aboveground improvement shall not be considered open space. Stormwater management features, such as lakes, ponds, and waterways, may be considered open space at the discretion of the Commission, provided that such areas are designed and maintained in a manner that contributes to open space and the aesthetics of the area.
2.1.155 Open space, public: An area within a development or subdivision designed and intended for the use and enjoyment of all residents or for the use and enjoyment of the public in general.
2.1.156 Orientation: The direction a building's primary elevation (also known as façade) faces.
2.1.157 Original tract: A unit of land which the owner holds under single or unified ownership, or which the owner holds controlling interest on the effective date of this Ordinance, where all land abutting said tract is separately owned by others, not related to or associated by business partnership with the owner.
2.1.158 Ornamentation: Decorative elements applied to a structure.
2.1.159 Outparcel: A lot within a planned center or a portion of a larger parcel that is reserved during development for sale and/or future development. In commercial developments, these lots are generally reserved along the frontage road for smaller businesses.
2.1.160 Owner: Any person, group of persons, firm or firms, corporation or corporations, or any other legal entity having legal title to land.
2.1.161 Package treatment plant: A sewage treatment facility, usually privately operated, typically having a treatment capacity of less than one million gallons per day. In most cases, a package treatment plant is considered a temporary means of wastewater treatment until connection to a public sanitary sewerage system is available.
2.1.162 Parking lot, accessory: A parcel of land or portion thereof used by a person, partnership, firm or corporation in any commercial or industrial zoning district exclusively for the parking of vehicles of its employees or customers and for which no charge is made.
2.1.163 Parking lot, commercial: A lot or building or portion thereof, other than an automobile sales lot, held out or used for the storage or parking of six or more motor vehicles for consideration where service or repair facilities are not permitted. Such parking lot or garage shall not be considered an Accessory Use; nor shall it be used for the storage of dismantled or wrecked motor vehicles, parts thereof or junk.
2.1.164 Parking lot, private: A parcel of land devoted to unenclosed parking spaces which may include partially enclosed one-story buildings, and where a charge is made for storage or parking of motor vehicles.
2.1.165 Parking space: Off-street space which is at least 18 feet long by nine feet wide used for the temporary location of one licensed motor vehicle having direct access to a street or alley, not including an access driveway. Every space shall be situated so that no part of any parked vehicle overhangs a public right-of-way. All parking space markings shall be laid out and restored as often as necessary to clearly delineate each parking space. Truck loading and unloading space shall not be considered a parking space.
2.1.166 Pedestrian way: A public right-of-way or private easement across a block or within a block to provide access for pedestrians and which may be used, in addition to providing pedestrian access, for the installation of utility lines.
2.1.167 Performance bond: A type of subdivision improvement guarantee in the form of a bond, secured by the subdivider from a bonding company, in an amount specified by the City's Engineer to cover the costs of required improvements, and payable to the City. The City may call in the performance bond in the event the subdivider defaults on required improvements.
2.1.168 Permitted use: A use by right which is specifically authorized in a particular zoning district.
2.1.169 Person: A natural human being, estate, association, firm, partnership, corporation, or other legal entity.
2.1.170 Personal care home: Any dwelling, whether operated for profit or not, which undertakes through its ownership or management to provide or arrange for the provision of housing, food service, and one or more personal services for two or more adults who are not related to the owner or administrator of the home by blood or marriage. Personal services include, but are not limited to, individual assistance with or supervision of self-administered medication and essential activities of daily living such as eating, bathing, grooming, dressing, and toileting. Also known as "Assisted Living Facility".
2.1.171 Personal property storage facility: A building or structure designed and used for the renting of space under a rental agreement that provides a renter access to rented space for the storage and retrieval of personal property. Residential use of storage units is prohibited.
2.1.172 Personal service establishment: A business providing personal, financial, technical or repair services, assistance or advice to individual consumers.
2.1.173 Planned unit development (PUD): A development constructed on a tract of at least ten acres, planned and developed as an integral unit under single ownership, and consisting of a combination of residential and nonresidential uses. (See also: Article 12).
2.1.174 Planning and Zoning Commission: The Planning and Zoning Commission of the City of Wrens, Georgia.
2.1.175 Planning and Zoning Commission member: Any person appointed by City Council to serve on the Planning and Zoning Commission.
2.1.176 Planting strip: The portion of the street right-of-way between the curb and the property line exclusive of the area occupied by the sidewalk.
2.1.177 Preliminary plat: A tentative drawing or map of a proposed subdivision. A preliminary plat is the basis for the approval or disapproval of the general layout of a land subdivision.
2.1.178 Professional engineer: An engineer duly registered or otherwise authorized by the State of Georgia to practice in the field of civil engineering.
2.1.179 Professional surveyor: A surveyor duly registered or otherwise authorized by the State of Georgia to practice in the field of land surveying.
2.1.180 Protective covenants: Contracts made between private parties as to the manner in which land may be used, with the view toward protecting and preserving the physical and economic integrity of a designated area.
2.1.181 Public hearing body: Applicable to City Council or the Planning and Zoning Commission.
2.1.182 Public improvement: Any drainage ditch, roadway, parkway, sidewalk, pedestrian way, tree, lawn, off-street parking area, lot improvement, or other facility for which the local government may ultimately assume the responsibility for maintenance and operation, or which may affect an improvement for which local government responsibility is established.
2.1.183 Public notice: A notice published once in a newspaper of general circulation in Jefferson County, Georgia, at least 15 days and no more than 45 days prior to a public hearing.
2.1.184 Recreation, active: Leisure activities that are facility oriented, such as swimming pools, tennis courts, and ball fields.
2.1.185 Recreation, passive: Leisure activities that are natural resource oriented, such as hiking trails, conservation areas, and nature preserves.
2.1.186 Recreation vehicle: A vehicle type unit primarily designed for recreation or temporary camping, travel or seasonal use, which has its own motor power, or is mounted on, or towed by another vehicle and has a living area of less than 500 square feet. This includes travel trailers, folding camper trailers, truck campers and motor homes.
2.1.187 Reservation: A method of holding land for future public use by showing proposed public areas on a subdivision plat.
2.1.188 Reserve strip: A strip of land across the end of, or along the edge of, a street, alley, or lot for the purpose of controlling access which is reserved or held until future street extension or widening.
2.1.189 Residence: Any structure in which one or more people legally dwell.
2.1.190 Residential development: Any group of lots or structures used or designed primarily for residences.
2.1.190A Retail Package Liquor Store: A retail business establishment owned by an individual, partnership, corporation, association, or other business entity that is primarily engaged in the retail sale of distilled spirits, malt beverages, and wine in unbroken packages, not for consumption on the premises and which derives from such retail sale of alcoholic beverages in unbroken packages at least 75 percent of its total annual gross sales from the sale of a combination of distilled spirits, malt beverages and wine.
2.1.191 Right-of-way:
(a) Generally, the right of one to pass over the property of another; or
(b) A strip of land acquired by reservation, dedication, forced dedication, prescription, or condemnation and intended to be occupied by a road, street, crosswalk, railroad, electric transmission line, oil or gas pipeline, water line, sanitary storm sewer or other similar use.
2.1.192 Right-of-way line: A strip of land occupied or intended to be occupied by a street, crosswalk, railroad, road, electric transmission line, oil or gas pipeline, water main, storm or sanitary sewer main, shade trees, or for another special use and owned by a state, county or municipality.
2.1.193 Roadway, traveled way or street surface: That portion of a road which is improved, designed, or ordinarily intended for vehicular use. Divided roads and roads with frontage or access roads have more than one roadway. On undivided roads and roads without frontage or access roads, the roadway width lies between the curb lines or between the pavement edges, whichever is appropriate.
2.1.194 Satellite dish antenna: A device incorporating a reflective surface that is solid, open mesh, or bar configured and is in the shape of a shallow dish, cone, horn or parabola. Such device is used to transmit and receive radio or electromagnetic waves between earth and/or orbitally-based equipment. This includes satellite stations, television satellite dishes, and satellite microwave antennas.
2.1.195 Scenic views and sites: Those geographic areas containing visually significant or unique natural features, as identified in the Comprehensive Plan, or by other reasonable means.
2.1.196 Screening: Either (a) a strip of land at least ten feet wide, densely planted (or having equivalent natural growth) with shrubs or trees at least four feet high at the time of planting, of a type that will form a year-round dense screen at least six feet high; or (b) an opaque wall or barrier or uniformly painted fence at least six feet high.
2.1.197 Sensitive natural area: Any area, as identified now or hereafter by the Georgia Department of Natural Resources, which contains one or more of the following:
(a) Habitat, including nesting sites, occupied by rare or endangered species;
(b) Rare or exemplary natural communities;
(c) Significant landforms, hydroforms, or geological features; or
(d) Other areas so designated by the Department of Natural Resources; and which is sensitive or vulnerable to physical or biological alteration.
2.1.198 Septic tank: An approved watertight tank designed or used to receive sewage from a building sewer and to affect separation and organic decomposition of sewerage solids, and discharging sewage effluent to an absorption field or other management system.
2.1.199 Service building: A building or structure located within a Manufactured Home Community offering a washer and dryer facility for the welfare and convenience of the residents of the Manufactured Home Community. Such Service Building shall not be made available for the use of any person not residing in the Manufactured Home Community.
2.1.200 Setback: (See: Building Line Setback, Section 2.1.37).
2.1.201 Shade tree: A tree in a public place, street right-of-way, or special easement, planted to provide canopy that will obscure the sun and heat from the ground.
2.1.202 Shoulder: That portion of a roadway between the outer edge of the paved surface or the curb to the inside edge of the ditch or gutter or original ground surface.
2.1.203 Shrubs: Self-supporting, woody species as normally grown in Jefferson County, Georgia.
2.1.204 Sidewalk: A hard-surfaced pedestrian access area adjacent to or within the right-of-way of a road.
2.1.205 Sign: Any writing, printing, lettering, painting, display, emblem, drawing or other attention-gaining device used to advertise products, goods, services or events, or to make anything known. Signs include but are not limited to murals, streamers, flags, wheels, propellers, or other artificial devices, figures, shapes, lights, exhibits, temporary banners, portable and mobile signs.
2.1.206 Sign, box cabinet: A sign being flat in appearance with little or no dimension. Box Cabinet Signs include flat signs either internally or indirectly illuminated and with or without frame.
2.1.207 Sign, freestanding box cabinet: Any Box Cabinet Sign unattached to a building and/or structure. Freestanding Box Cabinet Signs are prohibited by this Ordinance.
2.1.208 Sign, wall-mounted box cabinet: Any Box Cabinet Sign attached to a wall of a building and/or permanent structure. Wall-mounted Box Cabinet Signs are permitted under this Ordinance.
2.1.209 Sign, group: A sign advertising two or more businesses which is located on the same lot or two or more lots under the same or different ownership.
2.1.210 Sign, marquee: Any sign attached to or hung from a marquee.
2.1.211 Sign, nonconforming: A sign that, on the effective date of this Ordinance, does not conform to one or more of the regulations set forth in this Ordinance, particularly Article 17.
2.1.212 Sign permit: A permit issued by the Zoning Administrator that authorizes the recipient to erect, move, enlarge or substantially alter a sign.
2.1.213 Sign, temporary: A sign which either:
(a) Is not permanently attached to any structure, building, motor vehicle, or the ground; or
(b) Is intended for a limited display period covering a special event; or
(c) Is designed and constructed to be movable from one location to another.
2.1.214 Site plan: A legible, organized and approximate drawing of a residential, multi-family residential, institutional, office, commercial, or industrial development, showing the general layout of a proposed development including among other features the location of buildings, parking areas, buffers and landscaping. The site plan is the basis for the approval or disapproval of the general layout of a development.
2.1.215 Slope: Degree of deviation of a surface from the horizontal, usually expressed in percent or degree; the ratio of the difference in elevation between two points on the ground, and the horizontal distance between these two points. For purposes of determining steep slopes, slopes shall be measured between two points on the ground separated by 100 feet or more.
2.1.215A Solar Farm: A large-scale solar collection system placed in an area for the purpose of generating photovoltaic or thermal electric power principally for use off-site, or where the solar collection system is the primary land use on the parcel where it is located, or where the total area of a ground based or free standing solar collection system occupies more than one-quarter (¼) acre. This is also referred to as a "solar park", "solar power plant" or "solar photovoltaic farm".
2.1.216 Sovereign authority: The power of a governing body to administer public policy.
2.1.217 Spacing: The distance between buildings located on adjoining parcels (thus including Setbacks).
2.1.218 Specified sexual activities shall mean:
(a) Actual or simulated sexual intercourse, oral copulation, anal intercourse, oral-anal copulation, bestiality, direct physical stimulation of unclothed genitals, flagellation or torture in the context of a sexual relationship, or the use of excretory functions in the context of a sexual relationship, and any of the following sexually oriented acts or conduct: sodomy, cunnilingus, fellatio, pedophilia, lesbianism, homosexuality; or
(b) Clearly depicted human genitals in a state of sexual stimulation, arousal or tumescence; or
(c) Use of human or animal ejaculation, sodomy, oral copulation, coitus or masturbation; or
(d) Fondling of the human genitals, pubic region, buttocks or female breasts so as to arouse or excite the sexual desires of a patron; or
(e) Sexually oriented torture; or
(f) Fondling or other sexual contact with an animal so as to arouse or excite the sexual desires of a patron.
2.1.219 Specified anatomical areas shall mean:
(a) Less than completely and opaquely covered human genitals, pubic region, or anus; or female breast below a point immediately above the top of the areola; or
(b) Human male genitalia in a discernible turgid state, even if completely and opaquely covered.
2.1.220 Stable: Any building or premise where animals are kept.
2.1.221 Steep slope: Lands with slopes of at least 35 percent, or those slopes which can be calculated with aid of a United States Geological Survey 1:24,000, 7.5 minute quadrangle topographic map or other available topographic information.
2.1.222 Story: The space in a building between the surfaces of any floor and the floor next above or below, or roof next above, or any space not defined as a ground floor, mezzanine, balcony, penthouse or attic.
2.1.223 Street: Land between the street lines, whether improved or unimproved, shall be considered part of the street. A street is constructed and open to vehicle travel as approved by official action of City Council. A street is also an existing federal, state, county or municipal roadway, constructed and open to vehicle travel.
2.1.224 Street, collector: Unless otherwise defined by a Major Transportation Plan or Comprehensive Plan, a collector street is a public street whose function is to collect traffic from neighborhoods and local streets and which connects to another public street of equal or greater classification. A collector street also may provide direct access to adjacent properties.
2.1.225 Street, dead end: A street with no outlet at one end.
2.1.226 Street, industrial: A street of some continuity used primarily by all forms of commercial or industrial vehicular traffic and used for travel between commercial areas, residential areas and industrial districts or between industrial districts.
2.1.227 Street, local: Unless otherwise defined by a Major Transportation Plan or Comprehensive Plan, any public street, except an alley, collector street, or arterial street which has a primary function to provide direct access to adjoining properties and which serves a limited area only, usually a single land subdivision.
2.1.228 Street, major arterial: Unless otherwise defined by a Major Transportation Plan or Comprehensive Plan, a Major Arterial Street is a street connecting two or more cities or communities, connecting two highways of equal or greater capacity, or serving as the primary access to a large land area. A Major Arterial Street may also serve a large traffic generator (e.g., an industrial area) and perform a secondary function of providing local access.
2.1.229 Street, marginal access: A residential street parallel and adjacent to a major thoroughfare and which provides access to abutting properties with protection from through-traffic.
2.1.230 Street, perimeter: Any existing street to which the parcel of land to be subdivided abuts one side.
2.1.231 Street, private: A road or street that has not been accepted for maintenance by the City and that is not owned and maintained by a state, county, city, or other public entity.
2.1.232 Street, rural: A street supplementary to the major street system which primarily serves agricultural areas or other lands not subdivided for residential use.
2.1.233 Street, width: The shortest distance between the lines delineating the right-of-way of a street.
2.1.234 Structure: Anything constructed or erected with a fixed location on or in the ground, or attached to something having a fixed location on the ground. Structures include, but are not limited to, the following: site built buildings, industrialized buildings, manufactured homes, carports, billboards, swimming pools, advertising signs, satellite dishes and storm shelters.
2.1.235 Subdivider: Any Person who undertakes the subdivision of land, and any Person having such a proprietary interest in land to be subdivided as will authorize the maintenance of proceedings to subdivide such land under this Ordinance, or the authorized agent of such Person.
2.1.236 Subdivision: A division of a tract or parcel of land into two or more lots, building sites, or other divisions for the purpose of sale or building development, whether immediate or future, including but not limited to all division of land involving the dedication of a new street or a change in existing streets. The word "subdivision" includes re-subdivision and, when appropriate to the context, relates either to the process of subdividing or to the actual land or parcel which is subdivided.
2.1.237 Subdivision, major: A subdivision that involves any of the following:
(a) The creation of more than three lots;
(b) The creation of any new public streets;
(c) A planned development;
(d) The extension of a public water or sewer system; or
(e) The installation of drainage improvements through one or more lots to serve one or more other lots.
2.1.238 Subdivision, minor: A subdivision that does not involve any of the following:
(a) The creation of more than three lots;
(b) The creation of any new public streets;
(c) A planned development;
(d) The extension of a public water or sewer system; or
(e) The installation of drainage improvements through one or more lots to serve one or more other lots.
2.1.239 Tower: Any structure designed and constructed primarily for the purpose of supporting one or more antennas, including self-supporting lattice towers, guy towers, or monopole towers. The term includes radio and television transmission towers, microwave towers, common carrier towers, cellular telephone towers, and other similar structures. This term also includes any antenna or antenna array attached to the tower structure.

3.4.1 Public Notice. A public notice for all public hearings shall be published once in a newspaper of general circulation in Jefferson County, Georgia, at least 15 days and no more than 45 days prior to a public hearing concerning proposed Zoning Changes or amendments to this Ordinance including the maps thereto, setting the time, place and purpose of said public hearing.
3.4.2 Procedure. Public hearings shall be conducted by the Public Hearing Body and shall be governed by Section 3.4 of this Ordinance. Minutes of the meeting shall be taken by a Public Hearing Body member or his/her designee. Copies of any findings and decisions shall be available upon request to interested members of the public. The public hearing shall be called to order by the Presiding Officer, who shall summarize the requirements as to speakers' conduct and time limits.
3.4.3 Presentation of the Zoning Administrator. The Zoning Administrator shall report on the application, including the following: (i) the location of the property, the present use, and a description of the proposed amendment, Variance or change requested by the applicant; (ii) any report, investigation, or recommendation of the Zoning Administrator; and (iii) any additional information considered by the Zoning Administrator to be relevant.
3.4.4 Speakers. Each speaker shall speak only to the merits of the pending application and shall address his/her remarks only to the members of the Public Hearing Body. Each speaker shall refrain from personal attacks on any other speaker or any discussion irrelevant to the pending application. Speakers shall not duplicate previous comments, as repetition deprives other speakers of valuable time to provide new information. The Presiding Officer or his/her designee shall refuse a speaker the right to continue if the speaker, after once being cautioned, continues to violate any of the provisions of this paragraph.
3.4.5 Presentation by Applicant; Time Limits. The applicant or applicant's representative shall present and explain his/her application after being recognized by the Presiding Officer. The applicant will be allowed not less than ten minutes combined total to make his/her initial presentation and subsequent rebuttal, but the applicant and all supporters shall have a combined time limit of no more than 15 minutes.
3.4.6 Public Comments. After the applicant's presentation, interested persons who support the application, after being permitted to speak by the Presiding Officer, may address the proposed application by standing and stating their name, address, and interest and any comments on the pending application. Persons other than the applicant who support the application are allowed to speak in support of the pending application, subject to the 15 minute combined total time limit.
3.4.7 Opposition. Persons opposing an application are allowed not less than ten minutes total as a group (and in no event less than the combined time used by the applicant and other supporters), to address their opposition to the application. The opponents shall have a combined total time limit of no more than 15 minutes. It is suggested that the supporters, and opponents, each obtain one spokesperson to present their views. No individual except the applicant, a group representative, or the applicant's attorney shall speak more than one time on an application.
3.4.8 Applicant Summary; Deliberation. The applicant shall have an opportunity for brief summary remarks using any reserved time from his/her initial presentation, after which time the Presiding Officer shall close the public hearing. The Public Hearing Body shall then deliberate and take action on the application pursuant to the provisions of this Ordinance. Deliberation may include questions to applicants, supporters and/or opponents. Actions of the Public Hearing Body shall be by majority vote, a quorum being present.

(3) Covered front porches;
(4) Pillars or posts;

28: Commercial districts should have access from major traffic arteries; however, it is not the intent of this Ordinance to encourage the development of long, narrow strips of commercial development fronting on major arteries, often referred to as "strip commercial" areas. Strip commercial development leads to the eventual formation of commercial slums, damages the traffic carrying capacity of streets, increases congestion, is often incompatible with adjacent residential areas, encourages undue scattering of commercial facilities to the inconvenience of the public, and creates disproportionate costs in the provision of governmental services. Extensions of commercial zoning districts via amendments to this Ordinance should be made principally for the provision of planned, unified commercial areas, and not in such a way that strip commercial areas are encouraged. Extension of commercial zoning should only be made after careful consideration of compatibility with adjacent uses and whether or not other land is available which is already zoned for commercial use.

39: Except as otherwise provided, no structure or land shall, after the adoption of this Ordinance, be used and no structure or part thereof shall be erected, altered or moved unless in conformity with the requirements herein specified for the zoning district in which it is located. The provisions of this Ordinance, in their interpretation and application, shall be considered minimum requirements adopted for the promotion of the public health, safety, morals, convenience, order, prosperity and general welfare of the City.
40: Except as provided herein, no building or structure shall be erected on a lot unless such a building or structure, enlargement, addition or alteration conforms with the area regulations and setback requirements of the zoning district in which it is located.
41: No lot shall be reduced, divided, diminished or so maintained that the yards, other open space or total lot area should be smaller than prescribed by this Ordinance, nor shall the density be increased in any manner except in conformity with the regulations herein established.

43: Every building hereafter shall be located on a lot as defined herein. In no case shall there be more than one main residential building and its accessory buildings on one lot. Apartments, Townhouses, Condominiums are considered as one main residential building.
44: No dwelling unit shall be erected on a lot which does not abut at least one accepted public street for the minimum lot width for the applicable zoning district as provided in Section 5.7.

In all zoning districts, no construction, structures, fences, hedges, bushes, outdoor uses or other obstructions to a clear view which extend over three feet in height shall be permitted at any corner of intersecting streets where either or both of the streets are less than 60 feet in width. Exceptions may be made for utility pole lines, lighting standards, U. S. Postal Mail boxes, traffic signs, and trees. The branches of trees shall be kept trimmed to a height of eight feet above the ground. Buildings having nonconforming setbacks shall be excepted from the requirements of this Section.
In all zoning districts, where the aforementioned obstructions are in excess of three feet in height and where either or both of the streets are greater than 60 feet in width and these structures, shrubs or outdoor uses are of such character as to constitute a permanent, regular, or temporary obstruction to vision, they shall be set back at least 15 feet from the right-of-way line of each street at all intersections so as to eliminate hazards and/or nuisances to the general public.
46: At each end of a through lot there shall be a front yard of the depth required by this Ordinance for the zoning district in which each street frontage is located; provided, that one of the front yards may be utilized as a rear yard.
47: Any parcel of land including any interior streets and recreation areas, which are occupied by a group of dwellings designed as a unit, may be deemed to be one lot. Group housing consists of two or more residential buildings to be constructed on a lot at least one acre in area not subdivided into the customary streets and lots, and which will not be so subdivided, or where the existing or contemplated street or lot layout makes it impracticable to apply the requirements of this Ordinance to the individual building units in such group housing, the provisions of this Ordinance may be varied. This variance from the application of these requirements to such group housing must be done in a manner that will be in harmony with the character of the neighborhood and that will insure a lot area per family and a standard of open space no less than the amount required by this Ordinance in the zoning district in which the proposed group housing is to be located. All special exceptions, as provided in this paragraph, which existed at the time this Ordinance became effective, shall be regarded as non-conforming uses.

For protection against defects which occur within one year after acceptance of the dedication of the public facilities, the City shall require:
(a) Whenever occupancy, use or sale is allowed before the completion of all facilities improvements intended for dedication, then, the Performance Bond or the Surety that is posted shall guarantee that any defects in such improvements or facilities that appear within one year after the dedication of such facilities or improvements is accepted shall be corrected by the developer.
(b) Whenever all public facilities or improvements intended for dedication are installed before occupancy, use or sale is authorized, then, the Performance Bond or the Surety that is posted shall guarantee that any defects in such improvements or facilities that appear within one year after the dedication of such facilities or improvements is accepted shall be corrected by the developer.
(c) An engineer or architect retained by the developer shall certify to the City that all facilities and improvements to be dedicated to the City have been constructed in accordance with the requirements of this Ordinance.
