10.3.1 Initiation of Application. Applications for land subdivision shall be available in the City Clerk's office. Applications for land subdivision shall be accompanied by payment of a filing fee as established by the City Council from time to time.
10.3.2 Pre-application Conference. Prior to the filing of any application to subdivide pursuant to this Ordinance, applicants are encouraged to schedule and attend a pre-application conference with the Zoning Administrator or his/her designee. The purpose of the pre-application conference is to provide applicants with the best available information regarding development proposals and processing requirements, and to ensure the availability of complete and accurate information for review of said application. Upon request of the applicant, the Zoning Administrator will answer questions and provide any other information that must be submitted to satisfy application requirements.
10.3.3 Fee. The fee for applications to subdivide land will be established by the City Council from time to time.
10.3.4 Meeting Scheduled. Upon receipt of a completed preliminary plat application, the Zoning Administrator shall schedule the application for the next regular meeting of the Commission and shall forward all pertinent materials in the application to the Commission for review. A complete application for preliminary plat approval must be submitted at least 21 days before the regular meeting date of the Commission to be considered on that agenda. The Commission's review of and action on a preliminary plat shall be based on whether or not the preliminary plat meets the purposes and requirements of this Ordinance, and all other City Ordinances that relate to the proposed subdivision.
10.3.5 Complete Application. Any application for action under this Article must be complete before it shall be accepted for processing.
10.3.6 Application Contents. All applications for land subdivision shall include those items listed in Table 10.10.A. All applications shall be submitted to the City Clerk along with all applicable fees.
10.3.7 Withdrawal of Application. Any petition for an application to subdivide may be withdrawn at any time prior to the decision of City Council on said application by the person or entity initiating such a request, upon written notice to the Zoning Administrator. In the event of such withdrawal, no filing fee for the application will be refunded by the City.
10.3.8 Limitation on New Applications. In a case where an application to subdivide land is denied by the City Council, the same or substantially similar application shall not be eligible for resubmittal and reconsideration until six months has elapsed from the date of said denial.

10.4.1 Applicability. These subdivision regulations shall apply to all real property within the corporate limits of the City.
10.4.2 Land is One Tract until Subdivided. Until property proposed for subdivision has received final plat approval and said plat has been properly recorded, the land comprised within the subdivision shall be considered one tract, or as otherwise legally recorded.
10.4.3 All Land Subdivisions to Comply. No person shall sell, advertise, or offer to sell, by deed, map, plat or other instrument, any subdivided parcel of land which has not been subdivided in accordance with the requirements of this Ordinance. It shall be unlawful for any person to transfer or sell land by reference to, or by exhibition of, or by other use of, a plat of a land subdivision that has not been approved and recorded in accordance with the requirements of this Ordinance. The description of such land by metes and bounds in the instrument of transfer shall not exempt the transaction from the subdivision requirements of this Ordinance. No plat of land subdivision shall be entitled to be recorded in the Office of the Clerk of the Superior Court of Jefferson County and it shall be unlawful to record such a plat of land subdivision, unless and until it has been approved in accordance with the requirements of this Ordinance.
10.4.4 Preliminary Plat and Plans Required Prior to Construction. No person shall commence construction of any improvements on any lot prior to the approval of a preliminary plat, if required by this Ordinance, nor prior to the approval of construction plans and engineering plans for said improvements as required by this Article.
10.4.5 Building and Other Permits. No Building Permit or Certificate of Occupancy shall be issued for a building, structure, or use, nor shall any excavation, grading, or land disturbance applications be approved, on any parcel of land regulated by this Article that has not been approved in accordance with the provisions of this Article.
10.4.6 Public Streets and Lands. No land dedicated as a public street or for other public purpose shall be opened, extended, or accepted as a public street or other public land unless such improvements are constructed in accordance with the specifications of this Ordinance and said land and/or improvements are formally approved and accepted as public improvements by the City Council in accordance with procedures established in this Ordinance.
10.4.7 Appeals. Any person aggrieved by an interpretation or decision of the Zoning Administrator, City's Engineer, or other official responsible for the administration of this Article may file an appeal to the Commission in accordance with Article 24 of this Ordinance.
10.4.8 Exemptions from Plat Approval. The following types of land subdivisions, transfers, and sales are specifically exempted from the plat approval requirements of this Ordinance; provided, however, that such exemption shall not apply to land development requirements and improvement requirements established in this Ordinance:
(a) The sale of lots consistent with previously approved and recorded plats or deeds;
(b) The creation of leaseholds for space within a multiple-occupancy building or the division of property into leaseholds for commercial, industrial, or institutional use;
(c) The creation of leaseholds for the agricultural use of property where the use does not involve the construction of a building to be used as a residence or for other purposes not directly related to agricultural use of the land or crops or livestock raised thereon;
(d) Any division of land to heirs through a judicial estate proceeding, or any division of land pursuant to a judicial partition, or any division of land occurring from the foreclosure of a deed of trust; provided, however, that such exemption shall not require the City to issue permits if the resulting lots or parcels fail to meet any applicable regulations of the zoning district concerning lot size, lot width, and other dimensional requirements.

10.5.1 Block Length. Intersecting streets shall be provided at such intervals so as to provide adequate cross traffic. Blocks in residential subdivisions should not exceed 1,800 feet nor be less than 600 feet in length, except where topography or other conditions justify a departure from these standards. The Commission may require pedestrian ways and/or easements through the block to be located near the center in blocks longer than 800 feet. (See Figure 10.5.A).
10.5.2 Block Width. The width of the block shall normally be sufficient to allow two tiers of lots of appropriate depth. Blocks intended for business or industrial use shall be of such width as to be considered most suitable for their respective use, including adequate space for off-street parking and deliveries. (See Figure 10.5.A).

10.6.1 Natural Features and Assets. In the subdividing of land, due regard shall be shown for all natural features, such as tree growth, watercourses, historic sites or similar conditions which, if preserved, will add attractiveness to the proposed development and safety from hazards.
10.6.2 Access and Minimum Lot Frontage for Land Subdivisions. Each subdivision lot shall have access to a public street and a minimum lot width for the applicable zoning district as provided in Section 5.7 of this Ordinance; provided, however, that the local governing body may permit one or more lots to be accessed by private streets, as more fully specified in Section 10.14 of this Ordinance; provided further, that in the case of a lot accessed by a circular cul-de-sac, the minimum lot frontage may be reduced to 86 feet.
10.6.3 Adequate Buildable Area Required. Land subject to flooding, improper drainage or erosion, or that is unsuitable for residential or other use for topographical or other reasons, shall not be platted for residential use or for any other use that will continue or increase the danger to health, safety, or of property destruction, unless the hazards can be and are corrected. Each lot shall contain an adequate building site not subject to flooding and said building site shall be located outside of the limits of any existing easements or building setback lines required by the provisions of this Ordinance. (See Figure 10.6.A).
Figure 10.6.A Buildable Area
10.6.4 Lot Remnants Not Permitted. All remnants of lots below any required minimum lot size that may be required, left over after subdividing a larger tract, must be added to adjacent lots, rather than allowed to remain as unusable parcels. The Zoning Administrator may permit a lot remnant for a specific purpose such as a detention pond, provided that access and design is appropriate and the lot remnant is restricted to specific non-building use.
10.6.5 Service Areas. Commercial and industrial lots shall be adequate to provide service areas and off-street parking suitable to the use intended.
10.6.6 Lot Area. The minimum lot area shall not be less than that established by the zoning district in which the subdivision is located.
10.6.7 Lot Width. No lot shall have a lot width less than that established by the zoning district in which the subdivision is located. For lot widths, refer to Table 5.7.A for Residential lot widths, Table 6.4.A for Commercial lot widths and Table 7.4.A for Industrial lot widths.
10.6.8 Flag Lots. Flag lots are not permitted within the City.
10.6.9 Side Lot Lines. In so far as practical, side lot lines shall be at right angles to straight street lines or radial to curved street lines.
10.6.10 Corner Lots. Corner lots shall have adequate width to meet the front building setback requirements, if applicable, from all rights-of-way.
10.6.11 Double Frontage Lots. Double frontage lots or "through" lots should be avoided except where essential to provide separation of residential development from Arterial streets or to overcome specific disadvantages of topography or orientation. Double frontage lots with frontage on a major Arterial street shall allow space for screen planting along the lot line abutting the major Arterial street.
10.6.12 Survey Monuments For All Lots Required. For all subdivisions, a Georgia registered land surveyor shall install permanent survey monuments at all property corners and on land lot lines prior to final plat approval. Lot corners shall be marked with metal rods not less than one-half inch in diameter and 18 inches in length and driven so as to be stabilized in the ground. Permanent survey monuments shall be installed in accordance with the Technical Standards for Property Surveys of the State Board of Registration for Professional Engineers and Land Surveyors.
10.6.13 Lot Combinations. An existing lot line forming the boundary between two conforming platted lots located within the same subdivision or a lot line between lots or parcels that have merged to form one building lot may be removed or eliminated through a final plat revision process which conforms to the requirements of this Ordinance. In the case no final plat applies to the subject lots or parcels, a boundary survey and plat depicting all lots involved in the lot combination shall be required to be approved by the Zoning Administrator and recorded as a final plat. Such combination plat shall be titled with the same name as that of the original subdivision, if applicable, and shall indicate thereon that the re-plat is for the purpose of removing the lot lines between specific lots. (See Figure 10.6.B).

10.6.14 Boundary Line Adjustments. One or more existing lot lines forming boundaries between conforming platted lots located within the same subdivision, or one or more lot lines between abutting lots or parcels may be adjusted through a final plat revision process that requires the approval of the City Council and recording of a plat meeting the specifications of a final plat. In the case no final plat applies to the subject lots or parcels, a boundary survey and plat of the entire lots involved in the boundary line adjustment shall be required to be approved by the Zoning Administrator and recorded. Such plat showing said boundary line adjustment shall be titled with the same name as that of the original subdivision, if applicable, and shall indicate thereon that the re-plat is for the purpose of adjusting the lot lines between specific lots. (See Figure 10.6.C).

10.8.2 When Preliminary Plat Required. All major subdivisions, and any subdivision involving the dedication of a public street, shall require the submission of a preliminary plat to the Zoning Administrator for review and approval by the Commission. Prior to the issuance of any permit for land disturbance or for construction of any improvements, the Commission must approve the preliminary plat, if said plat is required.
10.8.3 Preliminary Plat Application and Specifications. Preliminary plat applications shall be made in accordance with requirements shown in Table 10.10.A and preliminary plats shall meet the minimum plat specifications shown in Table 10.10.B. Additionally, the words "Not for Final Recording" shall be noted on the preliminary plat.
10.8.4 Land Use Permit Required. Unless specifically exempted or otherwise provided by this Article, no building or other structure shall be erected, moved, added to, or structurally altered without a Land Use Permit issued by the Zoning Administrator. It shall be unlawful to use or occupy or permit the use or occupancy of any building, structure, land, water, or premises without a Land Use Permit for such use or occupancy. Unless specifically exempted or otherwise provided by this Ordinance, no land use activity including land disturbance shall be initiated without a Land Use Permit issued by the Zoning Administrator, and except in conformity with said Land Use Permit. It shall be unlawful to erect, move, add to, structurally alter any building or structure, use or occupy or permit the use of any occupancy of any building, structure, land, water, or premises, or initiate any land use activity that is in violation of an approved Land Use Permit.
10.8.5 Planning and Zoning Commission Review and Recommendation. The Commission shall consider all applications to subdivide land. It shall render a recommendation to the City Council on all such applications, and the Commission's action and recommendation shall be only advisory. The Commission may recommend approval, approval with conditions, or denial of the application. The Commission shall render a recommendation within 32 days after its meeting on the application has been held. The Zoning Administrator or his/her designee shall notify the applicant in writing of the Commission's action or recommendation within two days of the Commission's decision.
10.8.6 Disposition. Approval of a preliminary plat shall be valid for a period of one year, during which time a complete construction plan application must be submitted. If a completed application for construction plans is not submitted during this period, preliminary plat approval shall expire and be null and void.
10.8.7 Appeal. Denial of preliminary plat approval by the Commission may be appealed to the City Council.

10.13.1 Purpose. Minor subdivisions provide certain advantages, such as a shorter application process and less public scrutiny, that tend to favor their use over the filing of major subdivision applications. Given these advantages, the prospect exists that subdividers may seek to divide a tract of land via consecutive and/or contiguous minor subdivisions instead of filing for a major subdivision. It is the intent of the City Council to prohibit the practice of "chain" subdivisions where the same land owner subdivides land and then files minor subdivision applications on common contiguous parcels, which collectively total more than four lots. It is also the intent of the City Council to prohibit development of minor subdivisions adjacent to each other within a three-year time period in situations where part of an original tract of land is now owned by another person or entity and was transferred or sold to another owner with the apparent intent to circumvent the major subdivision process.
10.13.2 Common Contiguous Parcels Shown on Minor Subdivision Plats. Contiguous Common Parcels, as defined by this Ordinance, shall be referenced on all applications for minor subdivisions and Contiguous Common Parcels shall be considered part of any application for minor subdivision, for purposes of determining whether or not the division of land proposed is a major subdivision or a minor subdivision. Contiguous Common Parcels shall not be counted as lots in the case of a minor subdivision.
10.13.3 Limitations. Land within a minor subdivision, including all Contiguous Parcels owned by the subdivider, shall not be further divided for a period of three years unless a preliminary plat application is filed and approved as a major subdivision pursuant to the requirements of this Ordinance. If property proposed to be subdivided was part of an original tract, and if the property proposed to be subdivided abuts land that has been divided as a minor subdivision in the last three years, then minor subdivision of said property shall be prohibited. This provision shall not be construed to prohibit the approval of two contiguous minor subdivisions under separate ownership; however, this provision is intended to be construed liberally so that one property owner does not develop a minor subdivision on part of an original tract and transfer or sell another part of the original tract for the purposes of creating or developing minor subdivision within a three year period. It is the intent of this Ordinance that land abutting a minor subdivision that was owned by the subdivider shall not be subdivided as a minor subdivision for a period of three years, regardless of ownership.

10.14.1 Private Streets Permitted. Private streets may, upon application, be permitted by City Council within major subdivisions, subject to the requirements of this Ordinance. It shall be unlawful for any person, firm, or corporation to construct a new private street or alter an existing private street or to cause the same to be done without first submitting engineering and construction plans and obtaining approval from the Zoning Administrator and the City's Engineer in accordance with the requirements of this Ordinance.
10.14.3 Standards. All private streets shall be constructed in accordance with all standards for public streets as required by this Ordinance, applicable construction specifications of the City's Engineer, and as approved by the City's Engineer.
10.14.4 Street Names and Signs. Private streets shall be named, subject to the approval of the Zoning Administrator. The subdivider of land involving a private street shall install street signs with content containing the street name and the designation "private," as approved by the Zoning Administrator. The sign signifying the private street may be required by the Zoning Administrator to be a different color than that of street signs provided for public streets, in order to distinguish public or private maintenance responsibilities.
10.14.5 Easements for Private Streets. Easements for private streets shall be designated on final plats as general-purpose public access and utility easements, along with the name of the private street. At a minimum said easement shall be of the same width as is required for the right-of-way of a public street as determined by the City's Engineer, for the type of public street (local, collector, etc.) most closely resembling the proposed private street. Easements for private streets shall not be included in any calculation of lot size or density limitations established by this Ordinance. No lot shall be permitted to be divided by the general purpose public access and utility easement required and established for a private street. For private streets, the general-purpose public access and utility easement shall either:
(a) Be shown on the final plat in a manner that each lot fronting the private street extends to the centerline of the private street; or
(b) Be shown on the final plat as a separate parcel to be dedicated to a private Homeowners Association (i.e., not shown to be a part of any lot).
10.14.6 Maintenance. The City shall not maintain, repair, resurface, rebuild, or otherwise improve streets, signs, drainage improvements or any other appurtenances within general-purpose public access and utility easements established for private streets. A private maintenance covenant recorded with the County Clerk of the Jefferson County Superior Court shall be required for any private street and/or other improvements within general-purpose public access and utility easements established for private streets. The covenant shall set out the distribution of expenses, remedies for non-compliance with the terms of the covenant, rights to the use of easements, and other pertinent considerations. The covenant shall specifically include the following terms:
(a) The private maintenance covenant shall establish minimum annual assessments in an amount adequate to satisfy the costs of ordinary maintenance and describe procedures for approval of additional needed assessments. The Covenant shall also specify that the funds from such assessments will be held by a homeowners or property owners association in cases of a subdivision of seven or more lots fronting on a private street;
(b) The covenant shall include a periodic maintenance schedule;
(c) The covenant for maintenance shall be enforceable by any property owner served by the private street;
(d) The covenant shall establish a formula for assessing maintenance and repair costs equitably to property owners served by the private street;
(e) The covenant shall run with the land;

10.21.1 General Requirements. An adequate drainage system, separate and independent of any sanitary sewer system and including any necessary ditches, pipes, culverts, intersectional drains, drop inlets, bridges, etc., shall be provided for the proper drainage of all surface water for all subdivisions and land developments. Plans showing the size and location of all drainage structures shall be prepared by a registered professional engineer employed by the developer. The Zoning Administrator may require the use of on-site control methods such as retention or detention to mitigate the storm water and drainage impacts of the proposed subdivision or land development. The Commission shall not approve any preliminary plat of subdivision that does not make adequate provision for storm and flood water runoff channels or basins. No building permit shall be issued for any building within a subdivision or for the development of land, if there is not present throughout the subdivision or the land development an adequate system of drainage and storm water management.
10.21.2 Method of Design and Capacity. Storm sewers, where required, shall be designed by the Rational Method, or other methods as approved by the City's Engineer, and a copy of design computations shall be submitted along with required plans. Drainage improvements shall accommodate potential runoff from the entire upstream drainage area within the site and shall be designed to prevent increases in downstream flooding. Capacity for a ten year storm or rain shall be provided for all street drainage structures such as catch basins, inlets, cross drains, etc. Capacity for a 100 year frequency storm event shall be provided for all main drainage structures such as retention basins, principal storm sewers, and all types of flood protection works.
10.21.3 Location. Drainage facilities shall be located in the road right-of-way where feasible, and shall be constructed in accordance with the standards and specifications provided in this Ordinance, with approval of the City's Engineer. Catch basins shall be located at low points of streets. Where topography or other conditions are such as to make impractical the inclusion of drainage facilities within road rights-of-way, perpetual, unobstructed easements at least 15 feet in width for drainage facilities shall be provided across property outside the road right-of-way and with satisfactory access to the road.
10.21.4 Discharge. Drainage shall be designed so as to avoid concentration of storm drainage water from each lot or land development site to adjacent lots, land development sites, or vacant properties. Storm water shall not be discharged directly to perennial streams. It shall be directed toward natural drainages. If water must be discharged to a stream, the water quality flowing into the stream must meet or exceed the water quality of the receiving waters. The water quantity flowing into the stream must be evaluated to ensure the stream channel can accommodate the increased flows and not disrupt or degrade the ecology of the water body.
10.21.5 Grading and Site Drainage. Lots or land development sites shall be laid out so as to provide positive drainage away from all buildings, and drainage for individual lots or land development sites shall be coordinated with the general storm water drainage pattern for the area. Buildings and parking lots shall be appropriately drained so as to prevent damage to abutting properties or public streets. All disturbed or graded ground areas of a building site not used for buildings or open storage areas shall be appropriately stabilized and grassed or covered with plants or landscaping materials.
10.21.6 Cross Drainpipes. Where a watercourse separates the buildable area of a lot from the street by which it has access, provisions shall be made for installation of a culvert or other structure, the design of which shall be approved by the City's Engineer. Cross-drains shall be provided to accommodate all natural waterflow, and shall be of sufficient length to permit full-width roadways and the required slopes. Cross drainpipes shall have head walls of an approved type on inlet and outlet ends of the pipe. Pipe installed within the right-of-way shall be reinforced concrete pipe. All storm drainpipes shall have a minimum diameter of 18 inches. Storm sewer slopes shall be equal to or greater than one percent. All downstream receiving streams shall include a minimum 20 feet of rip rap.
10.21.7 Drop Inlets. Drop inlets shall be generally three-foot by three-foot boxes with two-foot by three-foot grates unless otherwise specified by the City's Engineer.
10.21.8 Curbs and Gutters Where Required.
(a) Curbs and gutters shall be installed in all major subdivisions in accordance with requirements of this Ordinance. Minor subdivisions shall not require curbs and gutters. All commercial and industrial subdivisions and land developments must have curbs and gutters, regardless of the size of the lots. When property fronting on an existing City street is subdivided or developed, and the subdivision or land development uses said existing street for access, then curb and gutter shall be required along said existing street along the entire property frontage of the subdivision. All curbs and gutters shall be constructed at the expense of the subdivider or developer in accordance with Georgia Department of Transportation standards.
(b) All streets and roads not required to include curbs and gutters shall be graded, paved, and drained and shall comply with all construction and drainage standards for ditches, slopes, and grassing in accordance with the provisions of this Ordinance.
(c) Curbs shall be concrete which shall be class A 3000 psi strength at 28 days. The typical curb minimum section shall be six inches by 24 inches by 12 inches. (See Figure 10.21.A).

Easements shall be provided for all drainage facilities as approved by the City's Engineer. 96: The purpose of Planned Unit Development (PUD) regulations is to encourage and allow more creative and imaginative design of land developments than is possible under zoning district regulations. PUDs are intended to allow substantial flexibility in planning and designing a proposal. This flexibility often occurs in the form of relief from compliance with conventional zoning ordinance site and design requirements. Ideally, this flexibility results in a development that is better planned, that contains more amenities, and ultimately a development that is more desirable to live in than one produced in accordance with typical zoning ordinance and subdivision controls. An intrinsic, and often neglected, premise upon which the approval of a PUD must be conditioned, is that while greater density or more lenient site requirements may be granted, the PUD should contain features not normally required of traditional developments. To enable a thorough analysis of a PUD, more information will be requested about the proposal than would be required if the development were being pursued under conventional zoning requirements.

12.7.1 Application for Approval. An application for approval of a PUD shall be filed with the Zoning Administrator and shall contain the following:
(a) Interest and Ownership. The applicant's name, address and interest in the application, and the name, address and interest of every person, firm or corporation represented by the applicant in the application; the concurrence of the owner or owners of the entire land area included in the special plan and a list of all encumbrances on such land; and sufficient evidence to establish that the applicants are all the owners of the designated land area, intending to develop the designated area, and have both the means and ability to develop the designated area.
(b) Plans for Building Development. Plans shall contain: (1) a description of the land area included within the special plan, with the boundaries and dimensions and present zoning classification of the area; (2) a description of the adjoining properties and the present zoning classification thereof; (3) all public or private easements and rights-of-way, both existing and proposed, within or bounding the designated area and the adjoining properties; (4) the location of adjacent buildings and the use of the land on adjoining properties; (5) necessary finished grades, curb cuts, driveways, off-street parking areas, off-street loading areas, sidewalks, open areas to be set aside for special purposes; (6) the location and height of proposed walls, fences, and screen planting; (7) the types of paving or other surfacing to be used in the various areas; and (8) such other site information as may be necessary to describe completely the proposed building development.
12.7.2 Compliance with State Laws. PUDs must comply with the applicable laws of the State of Georgia.
12.7.3 Review of Planned Unit Development by Commission. The Commission shall hold a Public Hearing concerning the PUD application in accordance with the provisions of this Ordinance. The Commission shall review each application and shall approve or disapprove the special plan; approval may establish conditions and limitations, which may include a performance bond. The Commission shall, within 30 days of its meeting, forward the application, together with its report of approval or disapproval to the City Council. The Commission shall notify the applicant in writing of the action taken on the application for the PUD.
12.7.4 Presentation of Planned Unit Development to the City Council. Once the PUD application has been forwarded by the Commission, the plan shall be presented to the City Council for final action. Action by vote shall be taken within 45 days after the application has been submitted to the City Council for consideration. If the Council fails to vote within the 45 day period, the time for Council action on the PUD will have expired and the PUD application will be considered disapproved. For the purposes of Section 12.7.8 of this Ordinance, the disapproval of a PUD application resulting from a non-vote of City Council shall be considered a "final act" of the City Council.
12.7.5 Registration of Planned Unit Development. Upon approval of a PUD, a copy of the development plan shall be filed with the Zoning Administrator. The development plan shall thereafter be binding upon the applicants, their heirs, successors, and assigns; shall limit and control the issuance and validity of permits and certificates, and shall restrict and limit the use and operation of all land and structures within the area designated in such PUD; provided however, that the Zoning Administrator may, upon a showing of engineering necessity, permit minor changes in the location of structure and site improvements if such minor changes will not change the character of the development Minor changes shall not: (a) increase the gross floor area of any structure; (b) change the intensity of use or ground coverage; (c) reduce the total building site area or the space between buildings; (d) change the ratio of off-street parking area and off-street loading area to gross floor area; or (e) otherwise cause the PUD to fail to meet the conditions specified in this Article.
12.7.6 Amendment or Withdrawal of Planned Unit Development. Pursuant to the same procedures and subject to the same limitations and requirements by which the PUD was initially approved and filed, any PUD may be amended or withdrawn, either partially or completely, if all land and structures remaining under such PUD comply with all the conditions and limitations of this Article and all land and structures withdrawn from such PUD comply with all zoning requirements and building regulations established by this Ordinance.
12.7.7 Fees. At the time of filing a PUD application, the party or parties proposing the PUD shall deposit with the City Clerk an application fee of $400.00 and an additional $50.00 per each additional acre over ten acres. The application fee is intended to cover the cost(s) of this procedure, and under no condition shall such sum or any part thereof be refunded for failure of such PUD to be approved by the City Council. The maximum application fee required shall not exceed $1,000.00 for a PUD or an amendment to a PUD.
12.7.8 One Year Limitation. Whenever a PUD is filed with the Zoning Administrator, and has been finally acted on by the City Council in accordance with the provisions of this Article, then the Commission and the City Council shall not consider a substantially similar PUD, for the same property, within a period of one calendar year from the date of the City Council's final action on said PUD.
